speaker: Doctor
text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To begin your evaluation for acute diarrhea, how long have your symptoms been present, and have you experienced any fever or blood in your stool?

speaker: Patient
text: 58-year-old female. The patient has been treated for community-acquired pneumonia with levofloxacin on the medical floor. She reports developing watery diarrhea with at least 9 episodes within the last two days, accompanied by lower abdominal discomfort and cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: The clinical picture of watery diarrhea developing after levofloxacin treatment for pneumonia strongly suggests *Clostridioides difficile* infection. Have you noticed any recent changes in bowel habits prior to this admission, and do you have a history of recent antibiotic use outside of this current hospitalization?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Watery diarrhea. I also have Lower abdominal discomfort, Abdominal cramping.

speaker: Doctor
text: DIAGNOSIS READY: Clostridioides difficile infection. Given the history of recent levofloxacin use and the classic presentation of watery diarrhea with cramping, I am requesting stool toxin testing and a C. difficile assay to confirm the diagnosis. REQUEST TEST: Stool_C_difficile_Toxin_Assay.
